title: midweek-ops-hackboard-capacity-alignment-brief
body:
Midweek ops hackboard notes 
Date: 2028-07-19 (captured during 11:00 sync)
Owner: Aisha Patel

Purpose: informal capture of capacity alignment ideas, running experiments, and immediate operational mitigations for next 72 hours. This is lightweight — use as a scratchpad and action list.

High-level summary:
- Regional demand spike predicted in APAC evening window (21:00-01:00 UTC) based on recent product release telemetry and a marketing push in SEA.
- We are short ~120 dedicated slots for p3-style instances during the predicted 4-hour peak if nothing changes.
- Current mitigation stack considered: micro-reserve lanes, soft-prewarming for hot models, KV-cache TTL tuning, and temporary routing to a lower-cost quantized variant.

Observations from last 24h:
- Steady-state fill rate for west-us is down 6% vs baseline (slot churn increased after rollout of balancer v3). See quick chart in PR #831.
- Preemption noise increased in europe-west3: correlated with cloud provider maintenance window; we saw ~18 abrupt evictions over 6 hours. Eviction rate spiked at 00:42 local.
- A micro-prewarm experiment (10% of requests, 160ms extra latency when cold) reduced cold-start errors by 72% for the chat workload but increased tail CPU by ~8%.

Experiments & probes (in-progress):
1) Kernel-probe v2 (Marco) — run a tiny sample of the new attention kernel on a 4k-seq model to check throughput under continuous-batching. Target run: 6 hours overnight. Metric: sustained tokens/sec and GPU SM utilization. (JIRA: INFRA-2147)
2) Micro-reserve lanes (Emily) — allocate 40 slots per APAC edge region as "soft-reserve": reclaimed if global demand requires. Goal: avoid hard prewarming cost while reducing spikes. Monitor reclaim frequency.
3) KV-cache TTL sweep (Samir) — test TTL 300s -> 900s for long-lived chat sessions in dedicated pools. Watch cache hit%, memory pressure, and perf counter for KV-evictions.
4) Quantized-fallback routing (Hannah) — set up policy to route to q4_0 variant when latency SLO at 99th breaches 600ms for more than 2m. Need canary and rollback hook.

Preliminary results (short window):
- Micro-prewarm: +72% cold error drop, +8% GPU tail — accept for 48h window while we measure economical impact.
- KV-cache TTL 900s: cache-hit increased ~11%, but memory pressure in eu-west3 nodes rose 14%; limits hit on one node leading to OOM-kill (investigate memory accounting).
- Kernel-probe: initial results show 5–7% improved tokens/sec for long-context but slightly higher transient memory allocs; need profiler traces.

Action items (owners and tentative due dates):
- Aisha: enable micro-reserve lanes in apac-a and apac-b for next 72h; monitor reclaim/saturation (due 2028-07-19 15:00). Linked: INFRA-2179.
- Marco: finish kernel-probe v2 run and upload perf traces to the PR; add flamegraphs (due 2028-07-20). GitHub PR: /pull/831.
- Emily: create dashboard panel for "soft-reserve reclaim events" and add alert if reclaim rate > 5/min (due 2028-07-20).
- Samir: revert KV-cache TTL change in eu-west3 and run memory-accounting job to capture allocations per process (due 2028-07-19 EOD).
- Hannah: draft canary config for quantized-fallback routing and run 10% traffic canary in dedicated pools (due 2028-07-21).

Decisions needed (sync before EOD):
- Approve 48-hour budget for micro-prewarm in APAC (rough estimate $5k/day) — Finance signoff needed.
- Agree to temporary priority bump for marketing release traffic vs internal batch jobs during the event window — ops to confirm.

Risks & notes:
- If provider evictions continue in europe-west3, we should consider failover routing to europe-west2 for specific latency-sensitive customers. That will require key rotation and brief config change.
- Memory accounting discrepancy: cancellation paths still holding references in kv-cache library (possible leak). Prioritize a minimal-repro test.

Quick links & references:
- Playbook snapshot: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFRA/pages/632918/priming-playbooks
- Kernel probe PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/831
- Related tickets: INFRA-2147 (kernel probe), INFRA-2179 (reserve lanes)
- Slack: #infra-priming thread (see pinned messages)

Unresolved questions / parking-lot:
- Should we change default KV-cache TTL for all dedicated pools or only on a per-customer basis? Pros/cons: global gives immediate benefits but increases memory surface; per-customer is safer but operational overhead.
- Can we add a cheap, pre-query classifier to route obviously short requests to the smallest model to reduce slot usage? Prototype cost/accuracy tradeoff?

Notes to self:
- Capture cost delta for micro-prewarm after 24h and 48h (compare token units + reserved compute hours).
- Remind release leads to throttle marketing bursts to 60% if reclaim rate spikes above threshold.

Status: draft hackboard — will be converted to a formal readout if we keep micro-prewarm for the 48h window.

End of notes.
